requirement: Implement SafeTaskRegistry wrapping Celery with in-memory eager configuration (task_always_eager=True, broker_url="memory://", result_backend="cache+memory://") and duplicate task registration detection. It must enforce explicit non-empty task names, prevent task shadowing by raising TaskCollisionError on duplicates, support task execution and retrieval, and provide clean registry reset.
skeleton: SafeTaskRegistry class with Celery app configuration, unique task registration decorator, and collision prevention.
caption: A Celery task registry that refuses to let two functions silently share one task name. TaskCollisionError subclasses ValueError. SafeTaskRegistry builds a celery application named som_tasks by default with eager execution enabled: task_always_eager follows the eager flag, task_eager_propagates is True so task exceptions surface to the caller, the broker is memory:// and the result backend is cache+memory://, so tests need no running broker. It tracks registered names in a set. register(name, bind=False, max_retries=3) raises ValueError for an empty or whitespace-only name, strips it, and raises TaskCollisionError when the cleaned name is already in its own set or already present in the application's task table; otherwise it returns a decorator that calls the application's task decorator with the explicit name, bind, and max_retries, records the name, and returns the task. get_task looks a name up in the application's task table, list_tasks returns the registered names sorted, and reset deletes each registered task from the application and clears the set. The fixture asserts that an eager task returns 12, that billing.generate_invoice is registered under its explicit name rather than the module path, and that a duplicate registration is rejected instead of shadowing the first task.

plan.intent: Register Celery tasks under explicit names without silent shadowing
constraints: The app runs tasks eagerly with an in-memory broker and propagates task exceptions
A blank name raises ValueError and names are stripped before use
A name already registered here or in the app's task table raises TaskCollisionError
Tasks are registered under the explicit name, not the module path
Reset unregisters every task and clears the set

rationale.teaches: A Celery task registry that is eager and in-memory by default, requires a non-empty explicit name, raises TaskCollisionError on duplicates, and unregisters tasks on reset.
rationale.why: Celery silently replaces a task registered twice under the same name, so a second definition shadows the first with no error. The fixture registers a duplicate and expects the collision to be reported.

ops.docstring: Safe Celery task registry preventing task shadowing and duplicate registration.

ops.source:
class TaskCollisionError(ValueError):
    """Raised when attempting to register a task whose name is already taken."""

candidates.why_wrong: eager defaults to False, so tasks are sent to a broker that does not exist and never execute in tests.
Duplicate names are accepted, so a later registration silently shadows the earlier task.
An empty or whitespace name passes the check, so a task with no usable name is registered.
The explicit name is not passed to the task decorator, so Celery derives a module-qualified name and collision detection never matches.
reset clears the local name set but leaves tasks in app.tasks, so re-registering after reset raises or shadows.
